title: Climb by the next number's factor
why: n odd ⇒ n+1 even composite, P(n+1)≤(n+1)/2; odd step then halving gives ≤(3n+1)/4<n (2^k−1 case similar): map contracts.

title: P(n)+P(n+1)−1
why: Collatz-type prime-factor dynamics; growth via prime chains p→p+P(p+1)−1, no contraction argument available.

title: Neighbours' largest factors
why: Twin-prime-type growth (n±1 prime gives 2n); proving finitely many cycles is Collatz-hard.

title: Last digits of consecutive largest factors
why: Joint residues of P(n),P(n+1) mod 10; only log-density results (Teräväinen-type) known for consecutive P; natural density open.

title: Prime continued fractions
why: Transcendence of a Hausdorff dimension of a CF Cantor set: no known methods even for E_{1,2}.

title: Prime plus two seven-free squares
why: Linnik p+x²+y² needed dispersion; adding digit restrictions on x,y requires Maynard-type Fourier input. Plausible but hard.

title: Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths
why: Infinite version of existing finite square-sum path Ramsey problem; not obviously trivial, no known reference.

title: Roth for seven-free numbers
why: Relative Roth in digit-restricted set; Fourier structure of missing-digit sets suggests density increment works, unknown in literature.

title: Partizan Prime Nim
why: Partizan subtraction game with infinite prime sets; claimed switch structure unverified and could fail; exploratory.

title: Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?
why: Decidability of (N,+,L) for sparse arithmetic sets tied to prime-pattern conjectures (cf. (N,+,Primes)); likely needs Dickson-type input.

title: Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N
why: Needs embedding bounded-degree hard graphs as induced square-sum subgraphs with poly bit size; plausible gadget work.

title: Fibonacci-sum chains
why: Fox–Kinnersley–McDonald–Orlow–Puleo (Fib. Quart. 52, 2014) characterize Hamiltonian paths in Fibonacci-sum graphs; computation shows N=F_k, F_k−1, plus 9,11.

title: Ramsey for prime sums of three
why: Three numbers: two share parity, their sum is even >2 (distinct), never prime. No such triple exists at all.

title: Graceful square-sum paths
why: N−1 distinct differences ≤N−1 must be {1..N−1}; difference N−2 needs N or N+2 square, impossible since N+1 must be square.

title: Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected
why: Hamiltonian-connected strengthening of prime circle (Greenfield); dense pseudorandom bipartite graph, absorption methods likely suffice.

title: No long climbs for 2P(n)+1
why: Consecutive increases force Cunningham chain p,2p+1,4p+3,… all prime; bounded K contradicts Dickson/Bateman–Horn (arbitrarily long chains expected).

title: Sofa in three dimensions
why: Same as existing "No prism sofa"/"Beat the prism" (3D square-pipe sofa, non-cylinder maximiser).

title: Self-avoiding polygon on the hat tiling
why: Same as existing "Self-avoiding walks on the hat tiling"; closed form unlikely to exist.

title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
why: Vanishing-forcing blow-up is close to the unforced NS problem; scaling does not trivialize forcing decay.

title: Prime-digit continued fractions in arithmetic progressions
why: Requires periodic CFs with prime quotients (no 1s) in every real quadratic field; McMullen-type arithmetic-chaos problem, all primes allowed eases it.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
why: Translative universal cover for diameter-1 sets; Lebesgue-type covering, likely mentioned in Brass–Moser–Pach; hard.

title: Entropy of the Prime Nim word
why: Grundy values appear unbounded (max 11 by 3000, open "Unbounded Prime Nim"); then block count is infinite and entropy undefined.

title: Self-avoiding walk on the hat tiling scaling
why: SAW ν=3/4 is open even on Z²; aperiodic version strictly harder.

title: Largest-prime-factor random walk
why: X_t is a nonnegative martingale (fair ±P, X−P≥0) moving by ≥2 until absorbed; martingale convergence forces absorption a.s.

title: Ising with prime couplings
why: Prime-spaced 1/r² couplings average r²J(r)~1/log r→0; ACCN/Newman–Schulman suggest no transition, claim possibly false.

title: Random hat tilings
why: Region family unspecified; hat tilings with reflections are hierarchical (zero plane entropy), so claimed positive entropy is ill-defined/likely false.

title: Stopping time law for P(n)+P(n+1)
why: Stopping-time law needs randomness of P(n),P(n+1) along orbits, plus global convergence; Collatz-type (Tao) difficulty.

title: Neighbour factors plus one
why: Same twin-prime-growth Collatz-type issue as the P(n−1)+P(n+1) map; distinct map, so not duplicate.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
why: Identical to existing "Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample".

title: Tileability by the spectre is undecidable for regions with holes
why: Statement fine (title says undecidable, M says NP-complete); gadget reduction for a fixed aperiodic tile plausible.

title: Sums of a square and a seven-free prime
why: Almost-all m²+p with Maynard seven-free primes; needs minor-arc bounds for digit-restricted primes, likely doable.

title: Seven-free squares density
why: Random-digit exponent is log10 9−1/2≈0.454, not 0.477; numerics to x=10^14 give 0.463 decreasing. Also near-duplicate "Seven-free squares".

title: Largest prime factor of n^n + 1
why: Primitive divisors give P≥2n+1; →∞ needs Stewart-type bounds with varying base, beyond current Baker methods.

title: Hadwiger number of square sums
why: Same as existing "Square-sum clique minors".
